stem.text: A particle moves in the xy-plane so that \( x(t) = - t + 4 \ln{\left(t^{2} + 1 \right)} \) and \( y'(t) = 2 e^{\frac{t}{2}} \sin{\left(t \right)} \) for \( t \ge 0 \). Using a calculator, find the acceleration vector of the particle at \( t = 1 \). Show the setup for the calculations, and give each value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The component given as a velocity is differentiated once, \( e^{\frac{t}{2}} \sin{\left(t \right)} + 2 e^{\frac{t}{2}} \cos{\left(t \right)} \) at \( t = 1 \) gives about 3.169.
The component given as a position is differentiated twice, \( - \frac{8 \left(t - 1\right) \left(t + 1\right)}{\left(t^{2} + 1\right)^{2}} \) at \( t = 1 \) gives about 0.000.
worked_solution.rule_named: second derivative of a position component

options.label: \( \left\langle 3.169, 0.000 \right\rangle \)
options.derivation: the two components written in the wrong order

options.label: \( \left\langle 3.000, 3.169 \right\rangle \)
options.derivation: each given component differentiated once, so the position component yields its velocity, not its acceleration

options.label: \( \left\langle 3.000, 2.775 \right\rangle \)
options.derivation: the velocity vector at the time reported as the acceleration
